isolation.note: Verified against OpenCode 1.18.31 (verified live during development): OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is honored as an inline config override; tools.{"*": false} disables every tool, permission.{"*": "deny"} denies execution, plugin [] and --pure drop plugins, mcp {} drops MCP servers, and a live probe confirmed the model can emit no executing tool calls. Residual limitation: OpenCode merges user-global config (~/.config/opencode) and managed settings that this harness cannot un-merge, so globally declared plugins/MCP servers may still be loaded (their execution remains denied). Claim: denied tool EXECUTION in a fresh session and fresh temp cwd; NOT a hermetic sandbox.

proposal.rationale: M=16 is a single row block; N=80 splits into 5 column blocks and K=32 into 2 K-steps of 16. Scratchpad rows 0-15 hold the current A K-tile and rows 16-31 the current B tile. Phase 1 loads A cols 0-15 once and computes all 5 N-blocks in overwrite mode (out_addr bit30=0, acc rows 0-15); phase 2 reloads A cols 16-31 and computes all 5 N-blocks in accumulate mode (bit30=1) onto the same accumulator rows, giving reduction in increasing K order. Every A and B element is DMA'd exactly once: 2 A tiles + 10 B tiles = 12 mvins = 3072 input bytes, which is the information-theoretic minimum. All computes use accumulated=false with preload-staged B tiles (the latched-B path is never needed since M has only one tile), bd_spad_addr is always GARBAGE_ADDR per the schema, and out_addr always sets bit31 (accumulator) and bit29 (full C width). Five mvouts store the finished 16x16 blocks at C element offsets n*16 with store stride 320 bytes (80 int32 per C row), followed by a final fence.

proposal.rationale: Fix for round 1: overwriting all five N-blocks onto accumulator rows 0-15 destroyed four blocks before mvout. Since 32 accumulator rows can hold only two pending 16-row N-block results, N=80 is processed in three groups {0,1},{2,3},{4}. Per group: with A K-chunk 0 resident in scratchpad rows 0-15, compute both blocks' K-chunk 0 in overwrite mode (block j into acc rows 0-15, block j+1 into acc rows 16-31); then load A K-chunk 1 into rows 0-15 and compute both blocks' K-chunk 1 in accumulate mode onto the same rows, yielding reductions in increasing K order; then mvout both blocks to C element offsets j*16 with store stride 320 bytes. Every B tile (2 K-steps x 5 N-blocks) is DMA'd exactly once (10 tiles); A chunks are loaded once per group (3x2 = 6 tiles) since K-chunk 0 and K-chunk 1 computes cannot overlap in the 32-row scratchpad (rows 0-15 A tile, rows 16-31 B tile). Total 16 mvin tiles = 4096 input bytes, the minimum given the accumulator-residency constraint; all computes use accumulated=false with preload-staged B tiles, bd_spad_addr is always GARBAGE_ADDR, and every out_addr/acc_addr sets bit 31 (accumulator) and bit 29 (full C width), with bit 30 distinguishing accumulate (3758096384/3758096400) from overwrite (2684354560/2684354576).
